questions.question: Recall the main characteristics of coal, petroleum, and natural gas as conventional energy source
questions.solution_html:
• Recall the main characteristics of coal, petroleum, and natural gas as
  • conventional energy sources. /[CO1]
  • Coal is a solid fossil fuel with a high carbon content and is mainly used for
  • electricity generation and industrial heating. Petroleum is a liquid fuel that is easily
  • refined into products like gasoline, diesel, and kerosene, making it highly versatile for
  • transportation and industry. Natural gas is primarily composed of methane and is
  • considered a cleaner fossil fuel due to lower carbon dioxide emissions when burned.
  • All three are non-renewable and take millions of years to form from ancient organic
  • matter. They are energy-dense and provide reliable, continuous power. However, their
  • extraction and use can cause environmental issues, including air pollution and
  • greenhouse gas emissions. These fuels have played a major role in global
  • industrialization and modern energy systems.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Breakdown the construction of a flat-plate collector and inspect how each component contributes to heat absorption.
questions.solution_html:
• Breakdown the construction of a flat-plate collector and inspect how each
  • component contributes to heat absorption./[CO4]
  • A flat-plate collector typically consists of a transparent cover, an absorber
  • plate, a fluid-carrying tube, insulation, and a casing. The transparent cover allows
  • sunlight to pass through while reducing heat loss to the environment. The absorber
  • plate, usually painted black, absorbs solar radiation and converts it into heat. The
  • fluid-carrying tubes transfer the absorbed heat to a circulating fluid, which carries it to
  • storage or directly to use. Insulation at the back and sides prevents heat loss from the
  • collector, improving efficiency. The casing protects the components from weather
  • while supporting the structure. Each part works together to maximize heat absorption
  • and minimize energy loss.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Examine the site selection considerations for a windmill.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the site selection considerations for a windmill./[CO4]
  • Site selection for a windmill requires an area with high and consistent wind
  • speeds to ensure maximum energy generation. The terrain should be free from
  • obstructions like tall buildings, trees, and hills that could reduce wind flow. Proximity
  • to power lines and the grid is important for easy transmission of electricity.
  • Environmental and social factors, such as wildlife impact, noise, and visual aesthetics,
  • should also be considered. Accessibility for construction and maintenance equipment
  • is essential. Local climatic conditions, including extreme weather events, must be
  • assessed to ensure safety and durability. Proper site selection directly affects the
  • efficiency, lifespan, and economic viability of a wind energy project.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Compare thermochemical and biochemical conversion processes.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare thermochemical and biochemical conversion processes. ./[CO4]
  • Thermochemical conversion involves using heat to convert biomass into
  • energy or fuels through processes such as combustion, gasification, and pyrolysis.
  • Biochemical conversion uses microorganisms or enzymes to break down organic
  • material, producing products like biogas, ethanol, or other biofuels. Thermochemical
  • methods are generally faster and suitable for dry biomass, while biochemical
  • processes are slower and more effective for wet organic matter. Thermochemical
  • processes often require high temperatures, whereas biochemical processes operate
  • under mild conditions. Thermochemical methods can produce a variety of fuels,
  • including syngas, char, and bio-oil, while biochemical methods mainly produce
  • methane and alcohols. Both methods help in energy recovery from waste and reduce
  • reliance on fossil fuels. Choice of method depends on feedstock type, desired product,
  • and economic feasibility.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Categorize organic materials based on their biogas yield potential. [5x3 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Categorize organic materials based on their biogas yield potential. ./[CO4]
  • Organic materials can be categorized into high, medium, and low biogas yield
  • potential based on their composition. High-yield materials include food waste, animal
  • manure, and energy crops, which are rich in carbohydrates and proteins. Medium-
  • yield materials include crop residues and green leaves, which produce moderate
  • amounts of biogas. Low-yield materials include lignin-rich materials like wood and
  • sawdust, which are difficult to digest and produce minimal biogas. The biogas yield
  • depends on factors such as moisture content, carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, and
  • biodegradability. Proper categorization helps in designing efficient biogas systems
  • and improving gas production. Mixing materials from different categories can also
  • enhance overall yield and maintain a balanced digestion process.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: List and show the advantages of non-conventional energy sources for sustainable energy development.
questions.solution_html:
• List and show the advantages of non-conventional energy sources for
  • sustainable energy development. [CO1]
  • Non-conventional energy sources include solar, wind, biomass, geothermal,
  • small hydro, and tidal energy. These sources are renewable and naturally replenished,
  • unlike fossil fuels which are finite. They produce little or no greenhouse gas
  • emissions, helping to combat climate change and reduce air pollution. Solar energy
  • can be used for electricity, heating, lighting, and water purification, especially in
  • remote areas. Wind energy provides clean power for residential, industrial, and
  • agricultural applications, depending on the location. Biomass energy utilizes
  • agricultural residues, municipal waste, and animal dung, converting them into
  • electricity, biogas, or biofuels, which also helps manage waste. Geothermal and tidal
  • energy provide stable, continuous power in suitable regions. Non-conventional
  • sources reduce reliance on imported fuels, enhancing energy security. They create
  • employment opportunities in installation, operation, and maintenance, supporting
  • local economies. Furthermore, these sources encourage sustainable development by
  • balancing environmental, social, and economic needs. With government incentives
  • and technological advancements, their efficiency and affordability are improving.
  • Overall, non-conventional energy is essential for a sustainable, low-carbon energy
  • future.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Compare the types of solar photovoltaic systems.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the types of solar photovoltaic systems./[CO4]
  • Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems convert sunlight directly into electricity using
  • semiconductor materials. PV systems are broadly classified into three types: on-grid
  • (grid-connected), off-grid (standalone), and hybrid systems.
  • On-grid PV systems are connected to the electricity grid. They supply electricity
  • directly to the grid and can feed surplus energy back, often earning credits or revenue
  • under net metering schemes. These systems do not require batteries for storage
  • because the grid acts as a virtual storage. They are suitable for urban areas and
  • industries where grid access is available. On-grid systems are cost-effective for large-
  • scale power generation and reduce reliance on conventional electricity.
  • Off-grid PV systems, also called standalone systems, operate independently of the
  • grid. They require batteries to store electricity for use during nighttime or cloudy
  • periods. These systems are ideal for remote or rural areas without grid access. They
  • are used to power homes, schools, irrigation pumps, and small community projects.
  • Proper sizing of solar panels and batteries is essential to meet energy demand reliably.
  • Hybrid PV systems combine solar PV with other energy sources such as wind
  • turbines, diesel generators, or battery storage. They provide continuous power supply
  • even when solar energy is insufficient. Hybrid systems are suitable for areas with
  • variable sunlight or critical loads like hospitals and communication towers. They offer
  • flexibility, reliability, and higher efficiency but are more complex and expensive.
  • PV modules can be monocrystalline, polycrystalline, or thin-film, affecting efficiency,
  • cost, and space requirements. The choice of system depends on factors like location,
  • energy demand, budget, grid availability, and reliability requirements. All PV systems
  • contribute to clean, renewable energy generation and reduce carbon footprints.
  • In conclusion, on-grid systems are efficient and economical for connected areas, off-
  • grid systems ensure energy access in remote locations, and hybrid systems provide
  • reliable and flexible power supply. The development of these PV systems plays a vital
  • role in sustainable energy generation, rural electrification, and reducing dependence
  • on fossil fuels.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Outline various applications of wind energy in industrial and rural contexts.
questions.solution_html:
• Outline various applications of wind energy in industrial and rural contexts.
  • /[CO4]
  • Wind energy is a renewable and sustainable source of power suitable for both
  • industrial and rural applications. In industrial contexts, large wind turbines generate
  • electricity for factories, warehouses, and commercial operations, reducing dependence
  • on conventional power. Wind energy can also supplement grid electricity, especially
  • in regions with variable demand. In rural areas, wind energy is widely used for water
  • pumping, irrigation, and livestock watering, helping farmers maintain sustainable
  • agriculture. Small wind turbines provide electricity for homes, schools, and
  • community centers in remote villages. Hybrid systems combining wind and solar PV
  • ensure continuous power supply in off-grid areas. Wind energy supports
  • decentralization, reducing transmission losses and improving energy reliability. It
  • creates local jobs in installation, maintenance, and manufacturing of wind turbines.
  • Environmentally, it reduces greenhouse gas emissions and helps conserve fossil fuels.
  • Additionally, rural communities become more energy self-reliant, promoting
  • economic development. Wind energy can also be harnessed for desalination, milling,
  • and cold storage applications, expanding its usefulness. The low operating cost after
  • initial investment makes it economically viable in the long run.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Examine how biomass can be converted into different forms of energy (solid, liquid, and gas) and outline the advantages of each method [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Examine how biomass can be converted into different forms of energy (solid,
  • liquid, and gas) and outline the advantages of each method. ./[CO4]
  • Biomass can be converted into solid, liquid, and gaseous energy forms
  • through various methods. Solid biomass includes wood, pellets, and briquettes, which
  • are directly combusted to generate heat or electricity. This method is simple, cost-
  • effective, and suitable for cooking, heating, and small-scale power generation. Liquid
  • biomass energy, such as biodiesel and bioethanol, is produced through
  • transesterification or fermentation. Liquid biofuels are easier to store, transport, and
  • use in vehicles and machinery, serving as a renewable alternative to petroleum fuels.
  • Gaseous biomass energy, produced via anaerobic digestion or gasification, yields
  • biogas or syngas. Biogas can be used for cooking, electricity, and heating, while
  • syngas can power engines and turbines. Each form of biomass energy helps reduce
  • greenhouse gas emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. Solid biomass is reliable
  • and locally available, liquid fuels provide high energy density, and gases are clean
  • and versatile. Biomass energy also promotes rural development by creating
  • employment in collection, processing, and distribution. By converting waste and
  • residues into energy, it supports a circular economy. Advanced technologies allow co-
  • generation of heat and power, improving overall energy efficiency. Using biomass
  • reduces environmental pollution and contributes to sustainable energy systems.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
